mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the location of the principal focus of a convex lens with that of a concave lens?

options.A: Both convex and concave lenses have their principal focus on the same side of the lens as the object.
options.B: A convex lens has its principal focus on the side opposite the object, whereas a concave lens has its principal focus on the same side as the object.
options.C: Both convex and concave lenses have their principal focus on the side opposite the object.
options.D: A convex lens has its principal focus on the same side as the object, whereas a concave lens has it on the opposite side.

mcqs.answer: A convex lens has its principal focus on the side opposite the object, whereas a concave lens has its principal focus on the same side as the object.
mcqs.explanation: For a converging (convex) lens, parallel rays converge to a real focus on the side opposite the incident light, so the principal focus lies opposite the object. A diverging (concave) lens forms a virtual focus on the same side as the object. Hence option B is correct; the other options describe incorrect locations.

mcqs.question: A convex lens has a power of +5 dioptres. What is its focal length?
mcqs.explanation: Focal length (in metres) is the reciprocal of the lens power: f = 1/P = 1/5 = 0.20 m, which equals 20 cm. Option A matches this value. The other options are mathematically inconsistent with the definition of power.

mcqs.question: Which of the following rays is NOT used in the standard ray diagram for a thin convex lens?

options.A: A ray parallel to the principal axis that passes through the focal point after refraction.
options.B: A ray passing through the optical centre of the lens and continuing undeviated.
options.C: A ray directed towards the focal point on the object side that emerges parallel to the principal axis.
options.D: A ray reflected from a plane mirror placed behind the lens.

mcqs.answer: A ray reflected from a plane mirror placed behind the lens.
mcqs.explanation: Standard ray diagrams for a convex lens use three principal rays: (i) parallel ray, (ii) chief ray through the centre, and (iii) ray through the focal point. A reflected ray from a mirror is unrelated to lens ray construction, making option D incorrect for lens diagrams. The other three options describe the accepted principal rays.

mcqs.question: An object is placed at a distance of 2f from a thin convex lens of focal length f. What is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.A: Real, inverted, and formed at 2f on the opposite side of the lens.
options.B: Virtual, upright, and formed between f and 2f on the same side as the object.
options.C: Real, upright, and formed at the focal point.
options.D: Virtual, inverted, and formed beyond 2f on the opposite side.

mcqs.answer: Real, inverted, and formed at 2f on the opposite side of the lens.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens, when the object is at 2f (twice the focal length), the image is formed at 2f on the other side, is real, inverted, and of the same size as the object. Option A correctly states these attributes; the other options describe situations that occur for different object distances.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a convex lens from a concave lens?

options.A: A convex lens diverges incident parallel rays, whereas a concave lens converges them.
options.B: A convex lens converges incident parallel rays to a real focus, whereas a concave lens diverges them to a virtual focus.
options.C: Both convex and concave lenses converge incident parallel rays to real foci.
options.D: Both convex and concave lenses diverge incident parallel rays to virtual foci.

mcqs.answer: A convex lens converges incident parallel rays to a real focus, whereas a concave lens diverges them to a virtual focus.
mcqs.explanation: Convex (converging) lenses bring parallel rays to a real focal point on the opposite side, while concave (diverging) lenses spread rays such that they appear to originate from a virtual focal point on the same side as the object. Option B captures this distinction; options A, C, and D invert or misstate the behavior.

mcqs.question: In a thin lens, the optical centre (O) is:

options.A: The geometric centre of the lens where the principal axis meets the lens surface.
options.B: The point where the principal focus is located.
options.C: The point midway between the two focal points.
options.D: The edge of the lens farthest from the object.

mcqs.answer: The geometric centre of the lens where the principal axis meets the lens surface.
mcqs.explanation: The optical centre of a thin lens is the point on the principal axis that lies at the geometric centre of the lens; rays passing through this point continue undeviated. It is not related to the focal points (options B and C) nor to the lens edge (option D). Hence option A is correct.

mcqs.question: A convex lens has a focal length of 10 cm. Where is its principal focus located?

options.A: 10 cm from the lens on the side opposite the object.
options.B: 10 cm from the lens on the same side as the object.
options.C: 5 cm from the lens on the opposite side.
options.D: 20 cm from the lens on the opposite side.

mcqs.answer: 10 cm from the lens on the side opposite the object.
mcqs.explanation: For a converging (convex) lens, the principal (real) focus lies on the side opposite the incident light at a distance equal to the focal length. With f = 10 cm, the focus is 10 cm behind the lens relative to the object. Option A states this correctly; the other options place the focus incorrectly.

mcqs.question: A thin concave lens has a power of –8 dioptres. What is its focal length?
mcqs.explanation: Focal length f (in metres) is the reciprocal of the lens power P: f = 1/P. For P = –8 D, f = 1/(–8) = –0.125 m. The negative sign indicates a virtual focus on the same side as the object, characteristic of a concave lens. Option A matches this calculation; the other options are numerically or sign-wise incorrect.
